title: Third-Party Evaluation: Blackbox Testing Access Protocol (Template)
content:
Purpose:
This template defines a repeatable, least-privilege protocol for granting third-party evaluators ("blackbox testers"/"external auditors") controlled access to Redwood Inference environments for the purpose of security, privacy and model-behavior testing. It is intended for use across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments, with clarifications for environment-specific constraints.

Scope:
- Applies to external vendors, academic partners, or independent researchers engaged to run blackbox tests that interact with our inference endpoints or observe runtime telemetry.
- Covers temporary access vectors, test data handling, telemetry collection, evidence preservation, and revocation procedures.
- Does NOT replace existing contractual DPAs, onboarding questionnaires, or infra-level SOC/ISO attestations; it supplements them with operational controls for active testing.

Risk Categories (examples):
- Data exfiltration: unauthorized export of customer inputs, responses, or internal telemetry.
- Model probing abuse: techniques that could be used to reconstruct proprietary weights or create poisoned inputs.
- Service disruption: load testing or malformed requests that degrade tenant performance.
- Privacy leakage: inadvertent exposure of PII in logs or debug captures.

Access Levels (pick one per engagement):
1) Observational API-only (lowest risk)
   - Evaluator may issue requests against a dedicated tenant API key with strict quotas and no access to internal logs or traces.
   - Response payloads truncated to remove debug metadata; request/response pairs scrubbed for customer identifiers.
2) Sandboxed Telemetry View
   - In addition to API access, evaluator is given read-only, aggregated telemetry dashboards or synthetic trace exports that are pre-scrubbed and sampled.
3) Isolated Test Cluster (highest fidelity)
   - Evaluator deployed within an isolated test cluster with synthetic datasets; access to limited runtime logs under NDA and technical controls (no privileged console).

Minimum Controls (required for all levels):
- Written engagement statement of work (SOW) and signed NDA + AUP (acceptable use policy) prior to any access.
- Scoped credentials with expiry (max 30 days by default) and per-evaluator rate limits enforced by token.
- Pre-engagement baseline scan: evaluator-provided tooling list and attack/test vectors overview.
- Test plan approval: Security & Product review required for modes 2 and 3.
- Telemetry redaction rules: automatic scrubbing of customer identifiers, IPs, and raw input tokens unless explicit customer test data has been authorized.

Provisioning Workflow (operational checklist):
1) Request submission: vendor fills access request form (link in linked_artifacts) with objectives, team contacts, proposed tests, and tooling.
2) Triage: Security evaluates risk level and assigns access level.
3) Contracting: Legal issues short-form amendment referencing this protocol; DPA/TOU checks performed.
4) Technical setup: infra issues time-bound token(s), sandbox endpoints, and synthetic dataset if required.
5) Smoke test: run baseline traffic to confirm rate limits and logging behavior.
6) Execution window: evaluator performs tests within agreed dates; all sessions logged and monitored.
7) Wrap-up: evaluator delivers final report, evidence bundle, and any exploit details; security performs forensic review.

Telemetry & Evidence Handling:
- Evidence collection must follow least-privilege: raw traces containing PII or customer identifiers must never be exported off-platform without explicit customer consent and a signed evidence release.
- All evidence exports must be stored in an encrypted evidence escrow bucket; access is logged and limited to named Security engineers.
- Retention: evidence retained for 90 days by default post-engagement then automatically purged unless retained for a live incident or customer request.

Allowed/Prohibited Tools:
- Allowed: L3 network sniffers inside isolated test clusters controlled by Redwood, blackbox test harnesses that only call public endpoints, fuzzing tools with agreed rate/volume.
- Prohibited without express exception: introspection agents, kernel debuggers, privileged container exec, or tools that attempt to extract model weights.

Data Minimization & Synthetic Data Guidance:
- When possible, supply synthetic datasets that mirror format and distribution of production inputs but contain no real customer content.
- If testing requires customer data, explicit customer authorization and a two-party evidence custody agreement are required; an authorized customer representative must sign off.

Incident & Abuse Response:
- Any indication of data exfiltration or abusive probing triggers immediate token revocation and a containment checklist.
- Security will initiate a forensics snapshot and notify Product + Legal within 2 hours of detection.
- If customer data exposure is suspected, follow the incident notification SLA in the DPA and contact affected customers per the disclosure playbook.

Attestations & Deliverables from Evaluator:
- Pre-engagement tool inventory and self-attestation of no prior involvement in adversarial ML reverse engineering.
- Post-engagement technical report with test vectors, findings, POC artifacts, and remediation recommendations.
- Signed certification that no raw customer data was retained off-platform.

Termination & Revocation:
- Access is revoked immediately upon: expiry, policy violation, or upon request by Legal/Security/Product.
- Evaluator must certify deletion of any derived artifacts and confirm deletion within 7 days; Security may request verification.

Approval Matrix (roles):
- Security Owner: approves risk rating and telemetry/redaction requirements.
- Product Owner: approves model/feature scope and synthetic dataset adequacy.
- Legal: approves NDA/SOW and any customer-data exceptions.
- Infra/OPS: provisions sandbox tokens and enforces rate-limits.

Signoffs (template):
- Security Reviewer: ____________________   Date: ______
- Product Reviewer: ____________________    Date: ______
- Legal Reviewer: ____________________      Date: ______
- Evaluator Representative: ________________ Date: ______

Annex A: Quick Operational Checklist (for Engineers)
- Confirm token scope & TTL set to engagement window.
- Configure WAF/ratelimiting and circuit-breaker thresholds for the token.
- Enable synthetic dataset if requested; verify no customer identifiers.
- Ensure log redaction filters are active for request/response capture.
- Point evaluator to aggregated dashboards; disable raw trace exports unless approved.
- Backup: create ephemeral forensic snapshot policy in case of suspected abuse.

Notes & FAQs (guidance):
- Q: Can an evaluator run high-volume load tests?
  A: Only in Isolated Test Cluster mode with Product approval and pre-agreed resource reservation.
- Q: Who pays for forensic review if abuse is detected?
  A: Redwood covers initial triage; if abuse is due to evaluator breach, costs may be billed back per contract.
- Q: Are model outputs considered customer data?
  A: Outputs derived from customer-provided inputs are treated as customer data and handled per DPA.

End of template.

This document is a living template; update version and linked artifacts when process or tooling changes.
